input: Draft a personal mission statement this weekend

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A mission statement covering all of life looks very different from one focused on career, leadership, or a specific role — the scope defines what content is even relevant.
Whether this is purely private or meant to be shared with others (a team, a coach, a partner) changes the tone, vulnerability, and level of polish needed.
Knowing what prompted this — a career transition, a life event, a self-development practice — reveals which values and themes are most pressing right now.
The available time window this weekend determines how deep the reflection exercises can go and whether multiple drafting sessions are realistic.
Mission statements range from a single punchy sentence to a structured paragraph with values and principles — the preferred style shapes the entire drafting process.
Understanding what 'done well' means — emotionally resonant, practically actionable, final-draft quality — sets the bar and prevents over- or under-engineering the output.
Whether the user wants a guided reflection exercise, a template, a writing prompt sequence, or a review of a draft they already started determines the immediate first step.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a personal mission statement this weekend
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to write a personal mission statement during the weekend, but key details about its purpose, depth, format, and process are unclear and will significantly shape the approach.

questions.title: What area of life should this mission statement cover?
questions.description: Determine whether the mission statement should span all of life (personal, professional, relational) or focus on a specific domain like career, leadership, or a particular role.

questions.title: Who, if anyone, will read or hear this statement?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a private document for the user alone, or something intended to be shared with a coach, team, partner, or public audience.

questions.title: What is prompting you to write this right now?
questions.description: Understand the triggering context — such as a career change, a major life event, a self-development program, or a recurring desire — to surface the most relevant themes.

questions.title: How many hours this weekend can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Establish the realistic time budget so the plan can be broken into appropriately sized reflection and writing sessions across Saturday and Sunday.

questions.title: Do you prefer one crisp sentence or a short paragraph?
questions.description: Determine the preferred format and length — from a single punchy sentence to a multi-part statement with listed values — to guide the drafting structure.

questions.title: What would make you feel this statement truly nailed it?
questions.description: Define the success criteria — whether that means feeling emotionally resonant, being practically actionable, reaching a polished final draft, or simply completing a first honest attempt.

questions.title: Do you have a draft started, or are you beginning from scratch?
questions.description: Find out the user's starting point to determine whether the immediate next action is a guided reflection exercise, a blank-page prompt sequence, or a review and refinement of existing material.
